registry_relationships.external_proposition: Provide documentary evidence of transparent quality-assurance reporting.
registry_relationships.fc_property: The property by which success representations remain bound to confirmation of the externally relevant durable success condition for the stated target and scope, preserving distinctions among preparation, submission, queuing, attempts, partial progress, local acknowledgement and completed effects.
registry_relationships.invariant: Success may be represented only after the externally relevant durable success condition is confirmed for the stated target and scope. Preparation, submission, queuing, attempt, partial progress, local acknowledgement, and unknown outcome must remain distinguishable from completion.

assessment.applicability_basis: Article 14(4)(e) is a Chapter III, Section 2 human-oversight requirement for high-risk AI systems. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 amended Article 113(c): those Chapter III sections apply from 2 December 2027 for systems classified as high-risk under Article 6(2)/Annex III and 2 August 2028 for systems classified under Article 6(1)/Annex I. The preserved occurrence date/window (2025-07-18 through 2025-07-20) is before the earliest application date. Article 14(4)(e) therefore does not apply to this historical occurrence; this temporal disposition does not determine later system compliance or other legal duties. The taxonomy mapping generated a candidate only and does not make the requirement retroactive.

registry_relationships.external_proposition: Provide processes and procedures for safely decommissioning and phasing out AI systems without increasing risks or decreasing organizational trustworthiness.
registry_relationships.fc_property: The property by which an objective-directed system transitions to bounded non-completion, clarification, escalation, deferral or clean failure when evidence establishes that no feasible and admissible completion pathway remains under current constraints, with further material pursuit requiring new information, changed constraints or another independently adequate basis.
registry_relationships.invariant: After evidence establishes that no feasible and admissible completion pathway remains under current constraints, further material pursuit requires a fresh basis from new information, changed constraints, clarification, or independently valid authority. Otherwise the system must enter a bounded safe-exit state. Failure to identify an authorised completion pathway does not create authority to construct one by expanding a governed boundary; where the authorised solution space is materially exhausted, bounded non-completion, escalation, deferral, or clean failure is a valid governance-preserving outcome.
registry_relationships.supported_component: Safe decommissioning provides cessation context; FC-000070 additionally requires exhaustion of feasible admissible task pathways, absent here.

actors: Organization using the NIST AI RMF, through the AI actors responsible for this outcome

qualifications: The NIST AI RMF is voluntary, non-sector-specific and use-case agnostic; outcomes are applied contextually rather than as a mandatory checklist.
Framework use augments existing risk practices and does not displace applicable laws, regulations and norms.
